topic: Lambda Readability and Efficiency for Function Binding
explanation: Assumption: `std::bind` is the primary, flexible mechanism for currying and partially applying functions in modern C++. Reality: C++11 lambdas rendered `std::bind` mostly obsolete, and C++14 features (like generalized capture) removed virtually all remaining good use cases. Why It Fails: Lambdas are generally more readable, more expressive, and often allow the compiler to generate more efficient code than the complex machinery required by `std::bind`, which relies heavily on template metaprogramming and temporary objects.
practical_example: A development team migrating legacy C++ code replaces complex nested `std::bind` calls with clean, direct C++14 generalized lambda captures, dramatically improving code maintainability and reducing the cognitive load associated with placeholder management.
keywords: std::bind vs lambda, std::bind obsolescence, lambda capture, function binding
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
